title: Late identification for a trip already superseded by a later one (part 2 of 2, second trip and the late identification)
description: Part 2 of 2 for O6, played after part1 against the same asset. This trip is a second, later trip that runs and closes normally before the identification arrives. The identification's claimed atSec is -600 relative to THIS file's trip start, standing in for a timestamp inside part1's trip window (real elapsed wall-clock time between the two playback sessions is not reproducible across separate fixture files, so this offset is descriptive rather than exact); it is not delivered until atSec 250, after this trip has already started and ended. Must prove: the trip-recency guard finds this second, later normal trip already exists on the asset and skips the asset write, while part1's trip is still linked (closed trip covers, flagged arrived_after_trip_ended), its own assignee still becomes A, and its two violations are still re-assigned to A. Must NOT change: the asset's current assignee (set by trip 2, or whatever stands after part1) must NOT be overwritten by this late identification -- that is exactly what the trip-recency guard exists to prevent -- and this file's own trip (trip 2) must keep its own assignee unchanged.

driver_identifications.note: claimed timestamp stands in for a point inside part1's trip window; delivered only after this file's own trip has already started and ended
